The rivers of India can be divided into two main groups: the Himalayan rivers and the Peninsular rivers. The Himalayan rivers are perennial, meaning they have water throughout the year. They receive water from both rain and melted snow from the lofty mountains.

The Ganga is the longest river in India, flowing about 2,525 km from the Gangotri glacier to the Bay of Bengal. The Peninsular rivers, such as the Godavari and the Krishna, are mostly seasonal because their flow depends on rainfall. The Godavari is often called the Dakshin Ganga because it is the largest Peninsular river.

Rivers have played an important role in the development of human civilisation. Many cities have grown on the banks of rivers.
